newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares stay calm amid summit flurry, end up.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares stay calm amid summit flurry, end up.

text.p: Dutch shares started the week with a record close, the eighth in the last eleven days, as the market felt the shove of a stronger dollar and supportive bonds.
The AEX blue chips index closed up 3.90 points at 849.99 after hitting an intraday peak of 850.68.
Dealers said market sentiment was quite positive, but some noted market players still uncertain on the exact outcome of the EU summit held today and tomorrow, limiting possible gains.
"We'll have to wait and see, but surely some positive things will come out of it (the summit)," one dealer said.

This afternoon's announcement that EU finance ministers had agreed a budget stability pact for countries joining a single currency and a resolution on jobs and growth, could not lift Dutch shares much further from their morning levels.
"We have reached complete agreement on the stability pact and the resolution for growth and employment," Dutch finance minister Gerrit Zalm said.
Film and musicmaker Polygram touched an intraday peak of 106.80 guilders in brisk trade, and closed up 5.40 guilders at 105.80.
"Today, it's just people running after this weekend's newspaper reports," one dealer said.
The share had risen 4.30 guilders on Friday, when investors applauded reports of a film contract between Polygram and British teen music group the Spice Girls.
Polygram's majority stakeholder Philips also ended higher, adding 4.40 guilders to close at 121.00 guilders.
"Philips's being pushed up by Polygram," one dealer said.
Brewer Grolsch ended up 3.10 guilders at 65.60.
Dealers said last week's announcement by Grolsch's Chairman Paul Snoep he intended to step down had induced buying.
"The fact he's leaving isn't taken as a bad sign," one dealer said.
Sector peer Heineken also closed up, adding 2.80 guilders to 345.50.
Builder IHC Caland, a midcap company, closed 2.90 guilders higher at 108.50 after the company said it had obtained orders worth 175 million guilders and repeated its profit forecast for 1997.
Ahold shares were unmoved by news the buy of Brazilian supermarket chain SuperMar by its unit Bompreco had been finalised. The stock ended down 1.70 guilders at 160.00.
